main.heading: The Financial Partner You've Been Looking For
paragraphs: Most small businesses and sole proprietors can't justify a full-time CFO — but that doesn't mean they don't need one. Whether you're scaling up, cleaning up your books, or planning for the future, you deserve the same quality of financial leadership that typical accounting firms reserve for their largest clients.

That's where we come in. Both co-founders, Lesley and Mark Hazleton, are PricewaterhouseCoopers alumni — Lesley on the accounting side, Mark on the consulting side. Combined with over 30 years of experience across Fortune 500 divisions and growing businesses, that depth of expertise is now available to your organization.

hero.label: About the Firm
paragraphs: Make Bold Solutions was founded on a simple belief: every business deserves access to experienced financial leadership — not just the ones big enough to be on a typical accounting firm's radar.

Led by Lesley Hazleton, CPA, an award-winning finance executive with over 30 years of experience, we bring the kind of hands-on financial guidance that small businesses, sole proprietors, and nonprofits have historically gone without — delivered with direct, senior-level attention.

We also believe in giving back. Lesley serves on nonprofit boards and provides pro bono financial guidance to organizations doing meaningful work in the community. Strong financial management shouldn't be a luxury — it should be available to every organization working to make a difference.

leader.name: Lesley Hazleton, CPA
leader.title: Founder & CEO

leader.awardTitle: Wichita Business Journal CFO of the Year, 2023
leader.awardDescription: Recognized for excellence in financial leadership and community impact
bio: Lesley is an experienced finance executive with over 30 years of hands-on leadership across public accounting, consulting, and multiple industries. She has served as CFO and senior finance leader for organizations ranging from $11M startups to $700M global divisions — and she brings that same depth of expertise to every client, regardless of size.

A PricewaterhouseCoopers alumna on the accounting side, Lesley went on to take on progressive leadership roles at Corning Inc., Goodrich, Elbit Systems of America, and FreeFlight Systems. She went on to serve as a Partner at SeatonHill Partners, a premier fractional and interim CFO firm, before co-founding Make Bold Solutions alongside her husband Mark — also a PwC alumnus, from the consulting practice — to bring that combined depth of expertise to smaller businesses.

Beyond her client work, Lesley is deeply committed to community service. She serves as Board Treasurer for Girl Scouts of the Kansas Heartland and as a Trustee for the Kansas Children's Service League Foundation — bringing the same rigor and care to nonprofit governance that she brings to her business clients.

cofounder.name: Mark Hazleton
cofounder.title: Founder & CTO
bio: Mark brings more than 30 years of software architecture and technology leadership to Make Bold Solutions. His background spans consulting, enterprise, and healthcare systems — with deep expertise in cloud architecture on Microsoft Azure, .NET application development, and AI-assisted delivery.

Make Bold Solutions brings financial clarity through CFO leadership and strategic guidance — and Mark ensures clients have the systems and tools to act on it. Whether that means evaluating a new platform, connecting business data to better workflows, or simply asking the right technical questions before a major decision, he bridges the gap between financial strategy and the technology that supports it.

Mark is the creator of DevSpark, an open-source framework for structured AI-assisted software development, and the founder of Project Mechanics, a delivery methodology refined across two decades of real engagements. He writes publicly about architecture and technology at markhazleton.com.

header.label: Recognition
header.heading: Wichita 2023 CFO of the Year
header.description: Lesley Hazleton, CPA, was honored by the Wichita Business Journal as one of Wichita's top CFOs in their 2023 CFO Awards program.

awardInfo.title: Wichita Business Journal CFO Awards 2023
paragraphs: The annual awards program, now in its 14th year, recognizes outstanding financial leaders in the Wichita region. Over 230 financial leaders have been recognized since the program's inception. The 2023 awards were presented at a luncheon on January 12, 2023, at the Hyatt Regency Wichita.
Honorees are selected through an independent process based entirely on merit, professional achievements, and contributions to the local community.

article.introParagraph: Winning the CFO of the Year Award in Wichita has been one of the most rewarding experiences of my career. It's not just an acknowledgment of professional success, but also a testament to the passion and resilience required to thrive in the fast-paced world of finance.

sections.heading: How I Found My Calling in Finance
paragraphs: My journey in finance began unexpectedly. I took an accounting class in high school and quickly discovered that I had an aptitude for numbers. Although what I learned was merely the basics of bookkeeping, I fell in love with the underlying theories. I realized early on that solving complex financial challenges was not only stimulating but deeply fulfilling.

Over the years, my passion for finance has grown through hands-on experience in public accounting, consulting, and manufacturing. Every step in my career reinforced that true problem solving lies at the heart of effective financial management.

sections.heading: The Role of Mentorship
paragraphs: One pivotal moment in my career was working with Steiner Eberle, the VP of Marketing at Corning Cable Systems. Steiner was more than just a mentor; he challenged me to see beyond traditional problem solving. He encouraged me to develop a financial vision and actively use my skills to shape the future of the business.
His guidance not only uncovered talents I wasn't aware of, but also provided me with opportunities to grow and take on responsibilities that have been integral to my professional journey.

sections.heading: Overcoming Challenges in a Rapidly Growing Environment
paragraphs: As a CFO, one of the biggest challenges I've faced is managing rapid growth. While growth is undeniably exciting, it brings with it a host of challenges that touch every part of an organization. Balancing working capital, addressing labor issues, and ensuring that every process is scalable in an ever-changing environment is no small feat.
Yet, it is precisely this intensity that makes the role so rewarding. Each obstacle has taught me the importance of adaptability, strategic planning, and collaborative leadership.

sections.heading: What I Cherish Most in My Career
paragraphs: Reflecting on my career, I believe my greatest professional achievement has been the ability to drive transformative growth. I've been fortunate to work in various sectors — from public accounting and consulting to manufacturing — and each experience has enriched my expertise.

My training in software integration, lean methodologies, and six sigma has allowed me to not only identify and solve complex issues but also to build a vision that resonates with my team. Collaborating and harnessing our collective strengths to overcome challenges remains my proudest accomplishment.

quotes.text: I took an accounting class in high school and realized that I had an aptitude. In college, I learned that my high school class was really just bookkeeping; but I loved the theory I learned. It really takes a problem solver to address complex accounting and finance issues.

I worked with Steiner Eberle, VP Marketing at Corning Cable Systems, early in my career. He encouraged me not only to act as a problem solver but also to proactively use my skills to develop a financial vision. His mentorship helped me grow in ways I never anticipated.

quotes.topic: On the biggest challenge as a CFO
quotes.text: Rapid growth is the biggest challenge I've encountered. Growth sounds exciting, but it impacts every facet of an organization simultaneously. It forces us to identify weaknesses, improve processes, and scale the business in an environment of constant change. Despite these challenges, the rewards are immense.

My greatest achievement has been learning how to apply my education, skills, and experience to drive growth and transform companies. Every organization has unique challenges, and I've learned to partner with my team to create a shared vision that leads us to success.

I love Wichita! Moving here has been the best decision I've made. Beyond reduced traffic and shorter commutes, it's the quality of life — from fantastic restaurants to vibrant arts and a welcoming community. Wichita is a place where people care, and that truly makes it feel like home.
